newsitem.title: USA: Idaho Pwr trims hydro estimate, still twice normal.
newsitem.headline: Idaho Pwr trims hydro estimate, still twice normal.

text.p: Idaho Power Co hydrologists revised their April-July inflow projection for the Brownlee Reservoir to 10.8 million acre feet (maf) from last month's forecast of 12.2 maf, the company said in a weekly newsletter.
A drier-than-normal February led to the revision, but projected flows are still more than double the 69-year median of 4.81 maf for the period.
Because of flood control requirements at the Snake River hydroelectric project, the water level at Brownlee continues to drop, the utility noted.
As of March 1 the water level was just 2,031 feet above sea level. By the end of the month the level is expected to drop to around 2,007 feet - or 70 feet below full.
Snowpack conditions in the mountains above the Snake River are 155 percent of the 30-year average, compared with 113 percent at ths time a year ago, Idaho Power said.
In an average water year, the Brownlee project provides about half of Idaho Power's electricity needs.
